commands.review_summary:
The branch adds heartbeat channel plugin pre-activation at gateway startup, adds an `allowBundledFallback` resolver option, changes heartbeat delivery target resolution to skip bootstrap and bundled fallback on the wake hot path, and updates outbound heartbeat tests.

PR surface: Source +61, Tests +23. Total +84 across 6 files.

Reproducibility: Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes from source: configure an external plugin heartbeat target only under `agents.list[].heartbeat`, then the PR's startup helper sees no default target while the runner still executes that per-agent heartbeat with hot-path bootstrap disabled.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) (fix(heartbeat): bootstrap plugin session targets, #93630) solved a real problem: when a user configured `heartbeat.target` to a channel id that was not in the built-in known-deliverable-channel list (e.g. a third-party plugin id), `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel()` returned `undefined` and the target was silently dropped to `"none"`.

The fix called `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` in the heartbeat delivery-target path. However, this triggers `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` → `loadOpenClawPlugins()`, which scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause analysis

The `bootstrapOutboundChannelPlugin` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts` has a `bootstrapAttempts` Set that caches per `(registryVersion, channel)` key:
- **Successful bootstrap**: key stays cached → subsequent ticks skip instantly
- **Failed bootstrap** (plugin not installed / config issue / transient failure): key is deleted → every tick re-runs the full plugin scan

This is the pathological case: a misconfigured or not-yet-installed heartbeat plugin channel causes repeated ~60s scans on every wake tick. The probe measurement confirmed:

```
Before (allowBootstrap: true,  no plugin): 73,308ms
After  (allowBootstrap: false, no plugin):   5.2ms
Pre-activation bootstrap (cold scan):           739ms (once at startup)
```

### When this bug is triggered

1. `heartbeat.target` is not `"none"` or `"last"`
2. The target channel is not in the active runtime registry
3. `heartbeat.to` is set (non-empty)

## Why This Change Was Made

Two-part fix:

### Part 1: Hot path optimization (original PR)

Three heartbeat-path call sites in `targets.ts` now pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`. A new `allowBundledFallback` parameter is added to `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` (default `true`) so hot paths can skip both the bootstrap scan AND the `getBundledChannelPlugin` lazy-load fallback.

### Part 2: Startup pre-activation (new — addresses review feedback)

A new `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` function in `src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.ts` runs **once at gateway startup** (in `activateGatewayScheduledServices`, before `startHeartbeatRunner`). It reads the heartbeat config and, for non-standard plugin channel targets, calls `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` to load the plugin into the active registry before the wake loop starts.

This preserves the delivery compatibility that PR #93630 established — external plugin channel heartbeat targets still get bootstrapped — but moves the bootstrap cost from the hot path (every tick) to startup (once).

Standard deliverable channels (telegram, discord, etc.) and targets of `"none"`/`"last"` are no-ops in pre-activation.

## User Impact

- **Normal deployment (plugin active)**: No change — plugin found in registry, <10ms resolution both before and after
- **Plugin not yet active** (external channel, delayed activation): Pre-activation resolves it at startup (~135–739ms once) instead of every heartbeat tick (~60s each). Delivery works.
- **Plugin not installed / misconfigured**: Fast fail at startup (best-effort bootstrap) and fast fail on hot path — no repeated scans

## Compatibility

- `allowBundledFallback` defaults to `true` — all non-heartbeat callers unchanged
- Pre-activation is a no-op for standard channel targets and `target: none/last`
- `resolveOutboundTarget` (general-purpose outbound) continues to pass `params.allowBootstrap` through transparently

## Evidence

### Unit tests (92/92 passed)
```
src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts                  85 passed
src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts    7 passed
```

### Probe timing (isolated vitest)
```
Pre-activation bootstrap (cold scan):  739ms (external-channel)
Pre-activation bootstrap (cold scan):  135ms (plugin-channel)
Hot path (allowBootstrap: false):       <10ms (registry lookup)
```

### Lint / type checks
```
oxlint:  clean
tsgo:    clean (check:test-types)
format:  clean (oxfmt --check)
build:   clean (pnpm build)
```

### Review response

ClawSweeper review ([#100377](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100377#issuecomment-4886719486)) identified that removing bootstrap from the hot path could drop delivery for external plugin channels not yet in the active registry. Startup pre-activation addresses this by resolving those plugins once before the wake loop starts, preserving the delivery compatibility of #93630 while keeping the hot path free of plugin scans.
